title: Inverted Full-Back Build-Up
definition: A tactical structure where full-backs move into central midfield zones to create numerical superiority and passing options during the initial build-up phase.
content: This concept involves full-backs, particularly those with high technical quality, abandoning their traditional wide defensive positions to invert into the midfield or first phase of play. By doing so, they create a local numerical advantage in central areas, facilitating short passing combinations and allowing the team to bypass high pressing lines. In the described scenario, the team utilized both full-backs for this role, with one acting as a defensive inverter in the first phase and the other potentially pushing higher or inverting depending on the center-back's ability to carry the ball wide. This flexibility forces opponents to track multiple potential threats, creating disorganization in their defensive shape. The inverted full-backs provide safe passing outlets for center-backs and midfielders, ensuring the team can maintain possession under pressure. This approach is particularly effective when the team has center-backs capable of playing the ball out and when the midfield requires additional support to retain control. It transforms the defensive line into a dynamic part of the attacking structure, blurring the lines between defense and midfield.
